subject: Redwood demo follow-up & observability discussion
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@datawave.ai>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@datawave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood demo follow-up & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — really appreciated the candid discussion about your latency and observability needs. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

- Objective: validate cost/latency and observability for a production inference path (text-generation + streaming, 2–4 rps per instance, 4–8s prompts)
- Hyperscaler comparison points you called out: pricing transparency, cold-start behavior, vendor lock-in, and traceability across request lifecycle
- Operational tooling you asked about: per-route dashboards, trace sampling, token-level cost breakdowns, and retention of audit logs for 1 year

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood provides a short technical test plan + temp API keys (hosted) so you can run latency/cost comparisons against your sample workload. (Target: 3–5k tokens/day for 48 hours)
2) We’ll stand up Redwood Console view for your account with a pre-built dashboard (latency percentiles, tokens/cost, per-route error rates) and a sample trace showing OpenTelemetry -> Redwood ingestion.
3) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) to walk through tracing integration and discuss Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.
4) Deliverables: one-pager comparison vs hyperscalers, observability playbook, and a draft proposal for committed capacity if the tests look good.

I’ve attached the one-pager that highlights key differences vs hyperscalers and a short observability playbook — see attachments. Rishi/Evelyn, can you confirm availability to kick off the test and issue temp keys?

Samira/Michael — can you confirm the sample prompt set & an available slot for the tech-deep dive later this week?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-onepager.pdf
Attachment: observability-playbook.pdf
From: Samira Khan <skhan@datawave.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@datawave.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we kick off the tests: 

1) For hyperscaler comparison, can you be explicit about what we should expect versus Bedrock/Vertex in terms of:
   - end-to-end tail latency at 99th percentile for streaming responses
   - token-level billing granularity (do you provide per-token cost breakdowns in the console)
   - ability to pin model variants and automatic fallback behavior during regional capacity pressure

2) Observability: our SREs want to see how traces map from our API gateway -> Redwood -> model execution and back. Do you ingest OpenTelemetry spans? Can we export traces to our Datadog/OTLP collector? Also want to confirm retention for traces/metrics and whether those are available in the console for at least 90 days.

3) For the test, we’ll provide a ~20 prompt set representing customer requests (avg 150 tokens, peak 800 tokens). We’re aiming to run a head-to-head against our current Bedrock configuration. Can Redwood capture per-request token counts and cost so we can do an apples-to-apples comparison?

We’re available for a deep dive Thu 3/5 or Fri 3/6 morning PT. Procurement will also want a draft of commercial terms if the test is positive.

—Samira
Sr. Product Manager, Data Platforms
DataWave Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@datawave.ai>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@datawave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up & next steps

Appreciate the specifics, Samira — good checklist. Quick answers and what we’ll deliver for the test: 

- 99p tail latency: We’ll capture a full percentile breakdown (p50/p90/p95/p99) for streaming and non-streaming routes. Expect lower cold-start variance vs hyperscalers for pinned Dedicated pools; hosted may have slightly higher cold-starts depending on model and sequence length. We’ll include a test run for both Hosted and our Dedicated trial to compare.

- Token-level billing: Yes — Redwood Console shows per-request token counts and cost attribution by route, model, and API key. We’ll provide the CSV export for your accounting team so you can do the precise cost comparison.

- Model pinning & fallback: We support model pinning by version and automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants or regional endpoints when capacity constraints are detected. We’ll include a simulated fallback scenario during the test window and show audit logs of the decision.

- Observability: Redwood ingests OpenTelemetry traces and can forward traces to an OTLP endpoint (Datadog/AWS X-Ray/Jaeger). Trace retention for the console (metrics & traces) can be configured; default is 30 days for hosted, and we can provide 90/365-day retention options for Dedicated or via log export.

Action items we’ll take this week:
- Rishi/Evelyn: create temp API key + test plan, stand up the console dashboard, enable OTLP forwarding to a sandbox endpoint, and prepare CSV export template.
- Marissa: send one-pager + draft commercial (attached).

I’ve attached the one-pager and observability playbook for your SREs. We’ll aim to have keys + dashboard ready within 24 hours after you confirm prompts.

Best,
Marissa
Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-onepager.pdf
Attachment: observability-playbook.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@datawave.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up & next steps

Looping in with technical details and what we’ll ship for the test. 

- Temp keys: I’ll provision a scoped API key limited to your test prompts (48h TTL) and a read-only console account that shows the prepared dashboard.
- Metrics/traces: we emit Prometheus-compatible metrics (redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket, redwood_tokens_total, redwood_request_errors_total). For traces, we accept OTLP over gRPC; you can forward to Datadog/your OTLP collector or let Redwood ingest and show the trace in the Console. Sampling is configurable; we’ll enable 100% sampling for the test window so you can inspect end-to-end traces.
- Dashboards: pre-built dashboard will include p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request histogram, model fallback events, and cost by API key. We’ll also export a CSV with per-request token counts and estimated cost.
- Test plan: run 48-hour baseline on your Bedrock host, then 48-hour on Redwood hosted, then a short (4–6h) run on a Dedicated trial (if you want to see pinning benefits). We’ll sync results and run a side-by-side diff.

Can you drop the prompt set (zip or shared Drive link) to the Drive folder and confirm an OTLP sandbox endpoint for forwarding? Happy to do the tech deep-dive Thu 3/5 10:30–11:00 PT if that works.

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer
